findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Route the reason-only administrative disposition through a GUARD FUNCTION with an unconditional call site (mirroring _ensure_duplicate_close_is_linked) rather than a new inline _completion_precheck branch, to respect the shrink-only, new-entry-locked complexity baseline; or explicitly document why the added branch stays under _completion_precheck's C901 ceiling.

search_files: _completion_precheck / close_precheck not present in .github/complexity-baseline.json (would need a NEW entry if it crosses the C901 threshold)
findings.finding: The plan proposes 'a NEW explicit _completion_precheck branch' for reason-only administrative classes, but the codebase's own docstrings (close_precheck.py:158-160, transition_close.py:311) state _completion_precheck sits at its recorded C901 ceiling in .github/complexity-baseline.json, which is shrink-only and locked against BOTH raised ceilings and NEW entries (complexity-baseline.README.md:13-14). The prior authors deliberately used a guard FUNCTION (_ensure_duplicate_close_is_linked) with an unconditional call site specifically to avoid adding decision points inside _completion_precheck. An inline branch contradicts that established, code-documented pattern and may push the McCabe count over threshold, forcing an unscoped refactor or an administrator baseline override the plan does not mention.
scenarios: make lint runs the complexity-baseline gate; the added branch raises _completion_precheck's McCabe count over threshold, requiring a baseline edit the shrink-only lock rejects.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the reason-only-administrative-skip decision as a small guard helper in close_precheck (e.g. _administrative_skip_verdict(...)) called unconditionally from _completion_precheck, keeping _completion_precheck's cyclomatic complexity at or below its current ceiling.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify where the new reason-only-administrative branch sits in _completion_precheck relative to the gate_enabled (:464-471) and force_close (:472-473) early-returns, so the signed disposition attestation is minted even when the completion-verification gate is disabled (mint the disposition verdict independent of gate state, mirroring the gate-independent write-side guard).

Plan step 5: obsolete/wontfix 'as-written would close UNSIGNED (the 738a trap)'
findings.finding: The plan's signed-disposition attestation (steps 4-5, AC4) can only be minted when the new branch runs, but _completion_precheck early-returns None when the completion-verification gate is disabled (gate_enabled check) and when force_close is set — both BEFORE any disposition logic. The plan does not specify placing the new administrative branch ahead of those early returns, so an administrative non-bug close on a repo with the completion gate OFF would close UNSIGNED, reproducing the 738a 'unsigned == forced/gate-off' trap that step 4 explicitly cites.
findings.location: Fix steps 4-5; close_precheck.py:464-473 (_completion_precheck gate_enabled + force_close early returns); AC line 4
scenarios: A repo with require_completion_verification_for_close disabled closes an obsolete task with --class obsolete --reason ...: write-side guard passes, but _completion_precheck returns None at the gate_enabled check, so no disposition verdict is minted and the close is unsigned — the very state AC4 requires to be RED
findings.suggested_fix: Route the reason-only administrative disposition (and the replacement-bearing disposition) through a verdict-minting branch that runs BEFORE — or independent of — the gate_enabled/force_close early returns for administrative classes, so the signed attestation does not depend on the completion gate being enabled; add an AC/test asserting an administrative close with the completion gate OFF still produces a SIGNED disposition manifest.
